study type: Cost-effectiveness analysis using a decision model
exposure: CYP2D6 genotyping to guide codeine use during breastfeeding
finding: Although not cost-saving, genotyping for CYP2D6 to guide codeine use during breastfeeding may be cost-effective for preventing neonatal adverse events, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of $10,433 Canadian dollars per adverse event averted.
